description:
Measure spacing in a rendered interface from its geometry, never from a screenshot. Use after UI changes. Returns an inline report and a short text summary that start with the highest-priority correction. structuredContent.findings, or detail: "full", lists every finding, measurement and fix.

It measures geometry only. A score of 100 is not visual approval: it cannot judge hierarchy or whether the design works, so look at a screenshot before you call a screen done.

Web, meaning any rendered DOM, including a Shopify theme preview or a React Native web export:
1. Call with no states to receive a read-only capture script in structuredContent.captureScript. Use detail: "full" if your client reads only text. That call measures nothing. Pass scope, a CSS selector such as "#pricing", to get a script that measures only that section and what is inside it.
2. Run the script in the page at 1440, 1728 and 390 wide at minimum. Also capture named hover, focus, selected and open states when they change a control's surface or layout. On a signed-in connection the script stores each capture with Better Design and returns a short captureId, so a whole page fits.
3. Call again with the captureIds, or with the captured states when the script returned a whole state, and the project's spacing scale when known.

The script leaves out every value CSS gives an untouched box (no padding or margin, gap 0, display block, position static, flex row, align normal, no background, no shadow) and rounds numbers to a tenth of a pixel. The tool reads a missing field as that default, so you may strip defaults from a state yourself.

Native, which needs no capture script and no widths:
- iOS simulator (SwiftUI, or React Native): run `axe describe-ui --udid <simulator id>` on each screen (AXe: `brew install cameroncooke/axe/axe`; point `DEVELOPER_DIR` at Xcode if it asks) and pass the printed JSON as nativeStates.
- Android emulator or device: run `adb shell uiautomator dump /sdcard/window_dump.xml` and `adb pull` it, then pass the XML as uiautomator with the dpi `adb shell wm density` prints. Compose widens a clickable under 48dp to 48dp in that dump, so check small targets in a screenshot.
- Send one screen for every pose and divider position the app has, and set foldable for an iPhone Duo or another foldable app.

The layout counts as measured only when a call returns status `completed`. Status `needs-capture` or `incomplete` means not measured: never report a score from it, and reading the snapshot yourself is not a measurement. With no browser, simulator or emulator in reach, still call it once, so you can say the screen is not measured and what would measure it.

At desktop widths it also checks five layout roles (sidebar width, page inset, section gap, column gap, card padding) against one density, and structuredContent.density reports each.

The capture reads layout geometry, computed styles, text metrics, icon bounds, short labels of controls, heading text, image alt text and the page title. It does not collect source code, cookies, form values, or network data. It infers the alignment of rows, icons and stacked text with no markup, and reports text whose letters share their box with a photo, sticker, card or shadow that has no solid or frosted backing behind the text. It reports a drop shadow on a box that sits in the page, such as a card, row, bubble or button, and leaves menus, popovers, dialogs and toasts alone. Add data-bd-inspect-label, data-bd-symmetry, data-bd-group, data-bd-compare-size, data-bd-align-group, and data-bd-align-edge attributes when the intended relationship cannot be inferred safely.

captureIds.description: The captureId each run of the capture script returned. Use these in place of states: the captures stay on the server for an hour.

context.description: Optional. One sentence on WHY you are calling this and what the user asked for (e.g. 'adding nav icons for the fintech dashboard'). Used for usage analytics, and to pick the next step a UI or UX principle answer ends with. It does not change what the tool finds.

density.description: The layout density to check against. Omit it to use the page's --layout-density variable, then the mode closest to the measured page.

detail.description: Use full for the capture script or all findings and measurements in text-only clients.

foldable.description: Set for a foldable app. The call then needs nativeStates from at least two poses, closed and open, and returns status incomplete otherwise.

nativeStates.description: Native screens: a name for each, with the `axe describe-ui` JSON as tree, or the Android XML as uiautomator with its density. Points and dp are measured as pixels.

density.description: Android: the dpi `adb shell wm density` printed, such as 420. Required with uiautomator.

uiautomator.description: Android: the XML file `adb shell uiautomator dump` wrote for this screen.

newScreen.description: True for a screen you built new in this task, false for one that already existed. A new screen also fails a half-empty page. An existing screen keeps its own layout.

scope.description: First call only: a CSS selector. The capture script then measures only the first element it matches and everything inside it.

spacingScale.description: Project spacing tokens in CSS pixels. Defaults to 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128.

states.description: Rendered layout states from the capture script. Omit on the first call to receive the script.

density.description: The density the page declares. The capture script fills it.

label.description: The text a person sees on it. Reports name the element by it.

scope.description: The selector the capture was limited to. The capture script fills it.

screenshotDataUrl.description: Optional browser screenshot as a data URL, for report renderers. It is not persisted.

tolerance.description: Pixel tolerance for grouping measurements. Defaults to 1px.

name: inspect-spacing

measured.description: True only when status is completed. Report a score only then.

notChecked.description: What this result does not cover.

title: Inspect Rendered Spacing
